{{< include _head.qmd >}}

Real music, analysed by experts, with the Roman numerals under the notes where each chord begins. Each piece has its own page. The
analyses come from [**When in Rome**](https://github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome), a collection of harmonic analyses gathered by Mark
Gotham and others.

## The pieces

- [**Bach: "O Haupt voll Blut und Wunden"**](bach-o-haupt.qmd) ("O Sacred Head, Now Wounded"), a four-part chorale from the *St Matthew
  Passion*, analysed by Dmitri Tymoczko. Short, with a key change at nearly every phrase.
- [**Beethoven: "Moonlight" Sonata, I**](beethoven-moonlight-1.qmd), the whole first movement, analysed by Tsung-Ping Chen and Li Su.
  Slow harmony, the Neapolitan, a tour of keys, and the form part by part.

## Reading the labels

A key followed by a colon (`d:`) means the music has moved to that key (capital letter major, small letter minor); the numerals after it
are in the new key. The figures are those of [Chapter 16](../figured-bass.qmd) (6, 64, 7, 65, 43, 42). ° is diminished and ø
half-diminished, as in the book. `V/iv` and `vii°7/V` are the secondary chords of [Chapters 17](../secondary-dominants.qmd) and
[18](../secondary-diminished.qmd); `N6` is the [Neapolitan](../neapolitan.qmd). A numeral sits under the bass where its chord starts;
where the bass holds a note through a chord change, the note is written as tied notes so the label has a place (it sounds the same).

## Using the scores

- **Play:** Space plays and pauses. Click a note to move there.
- **Resizing:** drag the line at the right edge of a score to make it wider or narrower (double-click it to reset); the bars re-flow to
  fit, and the size is kept for every score.
- **Keys:** above a score, the key strip shows every key the analyst names, in order, as wide as the time spent there. Click a key to light
  its bars and hear them.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For teachers

- **Sources:** the analyses are When in Rome's RomanText files, CC BY-SA 4.0, shown as they are (signs written as in the book: ° ø, figures
  run together). The scores are Craig Sapp's Humdrum encodings of public-domain editions, converted to ABC by
  `scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs`. That script also places each numeral at its bar and beat, and the browser test checks every
  converted note against the original encoding.
- **One analysis per piece:** the corpus has more than one analysis of both pieces (a second chorale analysis from the Bach Chorales
  Melody-Harmony Corpus, and Tymoczko's Moonlight). The site shows one; `build.mjs` can show more, as tabs, by listing them in `PIECES`.
- **Notes and other readings:** where an analyst left notes or alternative readings in the file, they are listed under the score.
- **Not edited:** the analyses are not this site's, and some labels follow the analyst's conventions rather than the book's (Cad64, Imaj7,
  I7).
- **More pieces:** the corpus has hundreds more (all the Bach chorales, Beethoven's sonatas and quartets, 19th-century songs). The same
  script can add them; each gets a page here.
:::
